cover.headline: Zaynich is a real scientific win, but the price already pays for more than management's own peak-sales guidance
cover.lead: Wockhardt sells generics in the UK and Ireland, insulin biosimilars in emerging markets and branded drugs in India, and in May 2026 won USFDA and Indian approval for Zaynich, the first antibiotic discovered in India to clear the FDA. After a decade of losses, profit turned in the Jul-Sep 2025 quarter: FY26 profit to owners was ₹213 cr and Q1FY27 ₹106 cr on 26% sales growth. Zaynich launches in India around Dec-2026/Jan-2027 and in the US in early 2027; management expects a slow first 12-18 months, a small loss and then a "hockey stick" towards US$1.5-2bn of peak sales. We forecast EPS of ₹21.2 / 22.0 / 33.5 for FY27-29E: Zaynich lowers EPS until FY29 (launch costs and amortisation). No broker standing on 30-Sep discloses a method, so we use **P/E**, the house and sector yardstick. Under the turnaround rule the window starts at the earnings break (1-Oct-2025, also the day after the Zaynich NDA was filed): Wockhardt's own forward P/E median of 66.7x × the nine pharma peers' +17.2% move over the same window = **78x Sep-28E EPS of ₹27.8**, a target of **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}): we initiate with HOLD.** Cross-checks: EV/EBITDA ₹2,014, DCF ₹670. Bull {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The science is genuine and de-risked in two markets
arguments.p: Zaynich (cefepime + zidebactam) is approved by the USFDA (30-May-2026, cUTI, priority review, QIDP) and CDSCO (27-May-2026); the EMA file is under accelerated assessment. It covers carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas, beat meropenem in phase 3, and has patent cover to 2038. Five in-house antibiotics have completed phase 3; Emrok and Miqnaf already sell in India.

arguments.h: But near-term earnings are the old business
arguments.p: Excluding Zaynich, EPS would be ₹25.6 / 28.7 / 32.9 in FY27-29E: launch losses and amortisation of the ₹1,055 cr capitalised Zaynich cost cut EPS by ₹4.4 and ₹6.7 in FY27-28E. The base business (UK generics, insulin, India) grows ~10% a year beyond FY27 and earns a 21-22% EBITDA margin that leaves most R&D capitalised.

arguments.h: A balance sheet repaired with other people's money
arguments.p: Debt fell from ₹3,582 cr (FY20) to ₹2,233 cr after an asset sale, a rights issue and two QIPs (₹2,216 cr of equity in five years); ~₹950 cr is still owed to the promoters, 18.8% of their shares are pledged, and a ₹3,000 cr fund-raise enabler went to the 2026 AGM. Three Indian plants remain on USFDA import alert since 2013-16.

arguments.h: Valuation: fair on the house method, rich on everything else
arguments.p: At ₹2,116 the stock trades at 76.2x Sep-28E EPS. Our 78x target multiple already includes the market's pipeline premium of the past year. Every cross-check is lower: EV/EBITDA ₹2,014, DCF ₹670, and a sum of the parts (base business at the peers' 34.5x P/E plus a Zaynich risked NPV) ₹1,310. Valuing the base business at the peers' EV/EBITDA, the price implies Zaynich peak sales of ~US$3.0bn, above management's US$1.5-2bn.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): Zaynich pre-launch costs, emerging-market insulin tenders, depreciation once the Zaynich intangible is capitalised.
Zaynich India launch (expected Dec-2026/Jan-2027) and US launch (early 2027): hospital formulary wins, first quarterly sales, launch-cost run-rate.
EMA opinion on Zaynich (management expects approval by end-2026); 7-8 emerging-market filings; any UK NHS subscription award.
HAP/VAP trial start for Zaynich (label expansion); Foviscu India NDA filing (planned Q3FY27); WCK 6777 phase 2 decision.
Use of the ₹3,000 cr fund-raise enabler; repayment or renewal of ~₹950 cr of promoter loans due by 20-Jun-2027.

sections.title: Three businesses under one roof: UK and Irish generics pay the bills, insulin grows, antibiotics are the bet

blocks.p: Wockhardt had ₹3,373 cr of revenue in FY26, 78% of it outside India. **UK** (39%; GBP 111mn): CP Pharmaceuticals in Wrexham makes hospital injectables and runs pharmacy, OTC and export channels (18% of its covered market, top-5 generic company); the site also fills and finishes vaccines under a 15-year collaboration with a global vaccine maker. **Ireland and Europe** (11%; EUR 35mn): Pinewood, the largest generic supplier to Irish hospitals (₹209 cr), plus continental Europe. **Emerging markets** (28%): mostly human insulin and glargine biosimilars sold to Brazil, Thailand, Egypt, Algeria, Malaysia and LatAm, often by tender. **India** (22%): a branded business (₹523 cr: diabetes, orthopaedics, pain, regenerative derma and the Emrok/Miqnaf antibiotics) and "India others" (₹217 cr). The **US** generics business was closed in July 2025.

Cutting across the regions are two specialty platforms: biosimilars (₹697 cr in FY26, ~21% of revenue, +27%) and novel antibiotics (Emrok, Emrok O, Miqnaf in India; Zaynich approved in May 2026). Together management calls them 23% of revenue. Wockhardt has 11-12 plants (India, UK, Ireland), two R&D centres and ~3,200 employees; three Indian sites are still barred from the US.

sections.title: History: import alerts, a fire sale to Dr Reddy's, four equity raises, and finally an approval

blocks.p: Wockhardt was a fast-growing exporter until 2013, when the USFDA put its Waluj (May) and Chikalthana (November) plants on import alert for manufacturing failures; Ankleshwar followed in 2016 and the US Morton Grove plant came under a consent decree. All three Indian alerts are still in force. To pay lenders it sold 62 Indian brands and the Baddi plant to Dr Reddy's for ₹1,850 cr in 2020: FY21's reported EPS of ₹57.1 is that gain (₹1,470 cr pre-tax, in discontinued operations); the continuing business lost ₹297 cr after ₹142 cr of exceptional charges. From 2021 to 2024 the company raised ₹2,216 cr of equity, which cut the promoters from 74% to 49%. The antibiotic programme survived all of it.

sections.title: Industry: superbugs are a big medical need but a hard market; insulin and UK generics are steadier

blocks.p: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR): bacteria that survive the antibiotics designed to kill them. Carbapenems are the last-line hospital antibiotics; carbapenem-resistant Gram-negative infections (Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, E. coli) have few options. Few companies still do antibiotic research: the chairman says eight companies started such programmes and Wockhardt is the only one to finish; big pharma largely left the field.

US: ~1.2mn Gram-negative hospital infections a year (cUTI ~600k, cIAI ~290k, HAP/VAP ~157k, BSI ~60k, other ~165k; company presentation citing an independent agency). New branded antibiotics together sell ~US$1bn a year (chairman); daily cost US$1,200-1,500. Recent launches have been slow: Shionogi's Fetroja (cefiderocol, approved 2019) was cited by an analyst at ~US$250mn; several small antibiotic developers went bankrupt after approval (e.g., Achaogen) because hospital uptake is slow and stewardship rules ration new drugs. India: 600-700k Gram-negative infections a year, 35-45% carbapenem-resistant (ICMR surveillance, company); ~300 infectious-disease specialists; emerging markets carry 70-80% of the global AMR burden (company).

UK NHS subscription model pays a fixed fee for approved antibiotics regardless of volume (chairman: up to GBP 20mn a year; NHS 2024 round contracts run Apr-2026 to Mar-2030); the US PASTEUR Act (subscription) was not law by 30-Sep-2026; QIDP status adds 5 years of US exclusivity. Insulin biosimilars in India and emerging markets: a US$5.6bn opportunity with 6-7 players (company); demand growing with diabetes; tenders make quarterly sales lumpy. UK generics: Wockhardt is a top-5 generic company with 18% of its covered market (hospital injectables, pharmacy, OTC, export); Pinewood is the largest generic supplier to Irish hospitals.

sections.title: Zaynich: approved in the US and India in May 2026, launching in early 2027, and priced like its rivals

blocks.p: Zaynich combines the old antibiotic cefepime with zidebactam, a Wockhardt molecule that both blocks bacterial enzymes and attacks the cell wall. It works against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales and Pseudomonas, the hospital superbugs for which few drugs remain. In the ENHANCE-1 phase 3 trial in complicated urinary tract infections (cUTI) it beat meropenem (Business Today: 89% vs 68.4% composite cure at test-of-cure; management cites ~20 points of superiority), and 85+ patients with no other option were treated under compassionate use. It is the first Indian-discovered new chemical entity approved by the USFDA.

bullets: **Price:** new US antibiotics cost US$1,200-1,500 a day, US$10,000-15,000 a course; Wockhardt will be price-neutral to them, i.e. it competes on efficacy, not on price. India at 20-25% of the US price.

**Ramp:** the chairman expects a slow start and a "hockey stick" after 12-18 months; his US director said new anti-infectives typically sell ~US$30-50mn in total over their first ~three years. Zaynich costs money until breakeven 12-18 months after launch (management).

**Peak:** management says US$1.5-2bn a year globally (no year given), the US ~40% of it, and a 20-25% share of resistant cases in the long run. The chairman also put today's US market for new branded antibiotics at ~US$1bn in total.
**Exclusivity:** composition patent to 2038; QIDP adds five years of US exclusivity. The US NDA and the US/EU business sit in Wockhardt Bio AG (85.85% owned).

**Competition:** Shionogi's Fetroja (cefiderocol) is the broadest rival and already in US hospitals; AbbVie's Emblaveo targets the same metallo-beta-lactamase niche. Zaynich's US commercial chief helped launch Fetroja.

sections.title: The base business: UK flat in sterling, Ireland and India growing, insulin doubling, US gone

blocks.h: UK (39% of revenue): a steady generics franchise, flat in sterling

blocks.p: CP Pharmaceuticals (Wrexham) and Wockhardt UK sold GBP 111mn in FY26 (₹1,318 cr), +3% in sterling and +13% in rupees. The business is hospital injectables (its specialty), pharmacy, OTC and export, with 18% of its covered market and 15 launches in FY26. Wrexham also fills and finishes vaccines: a 2020 UK-government line for COVID-19 vaccines and, since 2022, a 15-year collaboration with a global vaccine company (Serum) for up to 150mn doses a year, with profits shared 51:49 in Wockhardt Bio AG's favour. The split between vaccines and generics is not disclosed. Q1FY27 was GBP 27mn, flat on a year ago. We assume GBP 114 / 118 / 122mn (+3-4% a year) at ₹126 / 127 / 128/GBP.

blocks.h: Ireland and Europe (11%): Pinewood is growing

blocks.p: Pinewood, the largest generic supplier to Irish hospitals (liquids and creams), grew 16% in FY26 to ₹209 cr and 28% in Q1FY27 (₹64 cr). With continental Europe the region was EUR 35mn in FY26 and EUR 11mn in Q1FY27. Pinewood carries a EUR 25.6mn loan at EURIBOR + 8% with a EUR 16.6mn bullet in July 2028. We assume EUR 40 / 43 / 46mn.

blocks.h: Emerging markets and biosimilars (28%): the growth engine, but lumpy

blocks.p: Emerging-market sales rose 35% to ₹958 cr in FY26 and 64% to ₹263 cr in Q1FY27, almost all insulin (human insulin and glargine) under partnerships and tenders in Brazil, Thailand, Egypt, Algeria, Malaysia and LatAm. Biotech revenue (India + EM) was ₹697 cr in FY26 (+27%) and ₹236 cr in Q1FY27 (+112%). Management expects biosimilars to double in 24-36 months, with capacity doubling in 12-15 months and five insulin analogues after ~two years. Quarterly sales swing with tender timing (₹320 cr in Q4FY26, ₹263 cr in Q1FY27). We assume +22% / +18% / +15%.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Wockhardt has one real moat, its antibiotic discovery engine, now proven by a USFDA approval and protected by patents to 2038. Everything else is ordinary: a mid-sized UK/Irish generics business, a tender-driven insulin business against 6-7 rivals, and three Indian plants still barred from the US after a decade. Whether the science becomes a franchise depends on a US hospital launch by a company that has never run one.

sections.title: Twelve years in four acts: decline, a fire sale, survival, and a turnaround that is barely a year old

blocks.p: Wockhardt's revenue fell from ₹4,482 cr in FY15 to ₹2,651 cr in FY23 as USFDA import alerts (2013, 2016) shut it out of the US and it sold its best Indian brands to Dr Reddy's (2020) to pay lenders. It lost money before exceptional items and the sale gain in every year from FY17 to FY25; FY21's ₹686 cr "profit" was almost entirely the ₹1,470 cr pre-tax gain on that sale, booked in discontinued operations, while the remaining business lost ₹297 cr. Since FY24 the picture has changed: revenue grew 6%, 8% and 12%, the EBITDA margin rose from 3% (FY24) to 19% (FY26), and profit attributable to owners turned positive in FY26 (₹213 cr; ₹284 cr before ₹85 cr of exceptional charges). The quarterly turn came in Jul-Sep 2025: four profitable quarters in a row since, with Q1FY27 at ₹106 cr.

FY26 profit before exceptional items was ₹284 cr on ₹3,373 cr of revenue; the margin gain came from exiting loss-making US generics, cheaper materials (33.6% of sales vs 41.6% in FY24) and insulin volumes in emerging markets. Our FY27E EPS (₹{{F.eps.0|n1}}) is roughly Q1FY27 annualised less Zaynich launch costs; FY28E (₹{{F.eps.1|n1}}) barely grows because Zaynich adds amortisation and launch losses before it adds profit; FY29E (₹{{F.eps.2|n1}}) is the first year Zaynich pays.

sections.title: Margins: 19-21% now, but reported EBITDA leaves out most of the R&D bill

blocks.p: The company's EBITDA margin was 20.2% in Q1FY27 (₹188 cr) and 18.7% in FY26 (₹630 cr; Screener's basis 19.3%). Three things drove the rise from 5.4% in FY23: the exit from US generics (FY25 US revenue US$11mn, loss-making), lower material costs as insulin and UK injectables replaced low-margin lines, and about 50 cost projects. But the margin flatters the business in one important way: of an R&D spend of ~10% of revenue in FY26, only ₹120 cr (3.6%) went through the P&L; the rest (~₹215 cr) was capitalised as NCE development, building a ₹1,708 cr intangible under development (₹1,055 cr for Zaynich). That cost comes back as amortisation once the drugs launch. Quarterly margins also swing with emerging-market insulin tenders (23% in Q4FY26, 21% in Q1FY27).

sections.title: Cash: positive operating cash flow in only three of the last six years; shareholders funded the gap

blocks.p: Operating cash flow was −₹287 cr in FY21, ₹413 cr in FY22, ₹153 cr in FY23, ₹219 cr in FY24, −₹22 cr in FY25 and ₹390 cr in FY26; capex (including capitalised NCE development) ran at ₹166-365 cr a year. The shortfall, debt repayment and the antibiotic programme were paid for by selling assets (the India brands, ₹1,850 cr in 2020) and by shareholders: a ₹748 cr rights issue (FY22), a ₹468 cr QIP (Mar-2024) and a ₹1,000 cr QIP (Nov-2024 at ₹1,105). The share count rose from 11.1 cr to 16.2 cr. Working capital is heavy: inventory days rose to 286 in FY26 as insulin and UK volumes grew. Returns are still thin: ROE was 4.6% in FY26 and we forecast {{F.roe.1|pct}} in FY28E.

sections.title: Earnings quality: most R&D is capitalised, exceptional items every year, and a Swiss subsidiary with outside shareholders

bullets: **Capitalised R&D.** Total R&D was ~10% of revenue in FY26 (AR MD&A) but only ₹120 cr (3.6%) was expensed; the rest (~₹215 cr) was capitalised as NCE development. Reported EBITDA therefore excludes most R&D; it returns later as amortisation. Intangibles under development reached ₹1,708 cr (Zaynich ₹1,055 cr, Foviscu ₹350 cr, Miqnaf ₹201 cr), a key audit matter. If Zaynich disappoints, an impairment would hit book value directly.

**Exceptional items in five of the last six years.** FY21 −₹142 cr (continuing), FY22 −₹183 cr, FY23 −₹295 cr, FY24 −₹66 cr, FY26 −₹85 cr: deconsolidation of us subsidiaries (chapter 7, 11-jul-2025) and trustee settlement ₹-110 cr; new labour codes (gratuity/leave) ₹-10 cr; final settlement with dr reddy's of the ₹300 cr holdback under the 2020 business transfer ₹35 cr. We value on EPS before exceptional items (none forecast).
**Other income included one-offs.** FY26 other income of ₹111 cr included ₹55 cr of profit on asset sales and ₹15 cr of liabilities written back; interest income was only ₹7 cr.

**Minorities.** 14.15% of Wockhardt Bio AG (which holds the UK, Irish and EU businesses and the Zaynich US NDA) belongs to outside shareholders whom the annual report does not name. Bio AG lost ₹97 cr in FY26, so minorities absorbed ₹14 cr; once Zaynich earns money in the US, 14.15% of it leaks out. We forecast no minorities (≈₹1 of FY29E EPS).
**Tax.** FY26 tax was 16.3% because ₹118 cr of tax losses were used without a deferred tax asset; Q1FY27 was ~8%. The remaining loss pool is not disclosed; our 12% / 18% / 22% path is a judgement.

**Related-party flows.** Material RPT approvals sought with Wockhardt Bio AG (85.85% owned) of up to ₹1,000 cr a year incl. IP transfers at independent valuation (FY26: Wockhardt Ltd bought ₹278 cr of IP from Bio AG); overdue FEMA receivables from Bio AG flagged by the secretarial auditor.
**Audit.** MSKC & Associates LLP (appointed AGM 28-Jun-2024 for five years); unmodified opinion on FY26.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Nothing is hidden (it is all in the annual report), but reported EBITDA understates the true R&D cost, exceptional charges recur, and the IP sits in a subsidiary with unnamed minority holders and FEMA-overdue intra-group balances. The profit turn itself is real: four quarters of profit before exceptional items, positive operating cash flow in FY26 and an upgraded credit rating.

sections.title: Debt: down from ₹3,582 cr (FY20) to ₹2,233 cr, but ~₹950 cr of it is owed to the promoters

blocks.p: Borrowings peaked at ₹4,160 cr in FY17 and were ₹3,582 cr in FY20; the Dr Reddy's sale, the rights issue and the QIPs brought them to ₹2,021 cr (FY25). They rose again to ₹2,233 cr in FY26 as Wockhardt replaced working-capital lines with NBFC term loans (Tata Capital ₹334 cr at 10.55%, Axis Finance ₹182 cr at 11.25%), secured partly by pledged promoter shares. About ₹950 cr of the debt is lent by promoter entities at 5.9-12.3%, repayable by 20-Jun-2027 with an option to renew; the company quotes net debt/equity of 0.1 "excluding promoter debt". Liquid funds were ₹662 cr at Mar-26 (₹467 cr free, ICRA). ICRA upgraded the rating to A- (Stable) in May 2026: total debt/OPBDITA 3.4x, interest cover 3.1x. External repayments are ₹171 cr (FY27) and ₹198 cr (FY28).

bullets: **What you buy:** a ₹3,900 cr (FY27E) generics-and-insulin company with a 21-22% EBITDA margin and single-digit ROE, plus Zaynich: a genuinely novel, approved antibiotic with patents to 2038, launching into a hard US hospital market through a team that has never sold a branded drug there.

**What you pay:** ₹2,116, or 76.2x Sep-28E EPS, 96.1x FY28E and ~40x trailing EV/EBITDA. Valuing the base business at the peers' multiples, the price implies Zaynich peak sales of ~US$3.0bn, above management's own US$1.5-2bn. On our base peak (US$563mn) Zaynich is worth ~₹222 a share.

**Our target:** 78x Sep-28E EPS of ₹27.8 = {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}). The multiple comes from the stock's own year since the break, so it embeds the market's current enthusiasm; the cross-checks (EV/EBITDA ₹2,014, DCF ₹670, sum of the parts ₹1,310) are all lower.

**Triggers to watch:** the first two quarters of Zaynich sales in India and the US (H1CY27), the EMA decision, a HAP/VAP trial start, insulin capacity coming on stream, the use of the fund-raise enabler and the promoter-loan renewal in June 2027.

**How we would act:** Our ratings follow the upside to our 12−month target: BUY at +15% or more, HOLD between −5% and +15%, SELL below −5%. On our target that means buying below ~₹1,890 and selling above ~₹2,280. We would turn more positive on evidence of US hospital uptake ahead of the US$30-50mn three-year norm, not on approvals or peak-sales talk.

blocks.callout: **Bottom line:** Wockhardt deserves credit for Zaynich: it is the rare Indian new drug that cleared the FDA, and the base business has genuinely turned. But earnings to FY28 are the old business, and the share price already discounts a blockbuster. Our rule gives HOLD.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Wockhardt (consolidated, Rs crore; profit attributable to owners, see tools/authoring/WOCKPHARMA.patch.js). One reported segment, so the engine runs one revenue-growth path and one EBITDA-margin path; the build by region and the separate Zaynich line sit in `businessLines` (WOCKPHARMA.ctx.js checks they sum to model revenue and EBITDA). Forecasts carry no exceptional items and no minorities (14.15% of Wockhardt Bio AG; FY26 minorities absorbed Rs14 cr of losses). Valued on P/E on Sep-28E EPS (no broker note standing on 30-Sep-2026 discloses a method; P/E is the house and sector yardstick), multiple from Wockhardt's own forward P/E since the earnings break (1-Oct-2025) x the nine pharma peers' move over the same window (PLAYBOOK §7c turnaround rule).
assumptions._revenueWhy: Built by region (businessLines; the script checks the sum). FY26 base Rs3,373 cr = UK Rs1,318 cr (GBP 111mn) + Ireland/Europe Rs357 cr (EUR 35mn) + India branded Rs523 cr + India others Rs217 cr + emerging markets Rs958 cr. FY27E Rs3,881 cr (+15.1%): UK GBP 114mn at Rs126 (Q1FY27 GBP 27mn, flat in sterling; Rs127/GBP), Europe EUR 40mn at Rs110 (Q1 EUR 11mn, Ireland +28%), India branded +16% (Q1 +21%; Emrok +29%, Miqnaf, diabetes, regenerative derma), India others Rs205 cr (FY26 Rs217 cr, Q1 Rs46 cr, falling), emerging markets +22% (Q1 +64% on insulin; FY26 +35%; tender-driven and lumpy, Q4FY26 Rs320 cr vs Q1FY27 Rs263 cr), Zaynich Rs24 cr (India launch Dec-26/Jan-27, US stocking from early 2027). FY28E +16.0% (base +10.4%, Zaynich Rs243 cr) and FY29E +16.3% (base +9.5%, Zaynich Rs575 cr): biosimilars doubling in 24-36 months (management) drives emerging markets +18% / +15%; UK +3-4% in sterling. Management's press-reported ambition of Rs6,000 cr by FY28 is well above our Rs4,500 cr.

businessLines._why: FY26 by region from the Q4FY26 press release (4-May-2026). Rupee rates: UK FY26 Rs118.7/GBP (Rs1,318 cr / GBP 111mn), Q1FY27 Rs127; Europe FY26 Rs102/EUR, Q1FY27 ~Rs110. Zaynich: India (Rs cr) from launch around Dec-2026/Jan-2027, priced at 20-25% of the US (management: 75-80% discount); US in USD mn from early 2027 (management: new anti-infectives do ~US$30-50mn collectively in their first ~3 years; price-neutral to rivals at US$10-15k a course); EU + emerging markets from FY28 (EMA approval expected by end-2026; 7-8 emerging markets in 18-24 months). No UK NHS subscription income is assumed (no award found by 30-Sep-2026).

margin._why: EBITDA on Screener's basis (FY26 Rs652 cr = 19.3%; company basis Rs630 cr after R&D). Base business (ex-Zaynich) 21.3% / 21.8% / 22.3%: Q1FY27 was 20.7% (Screener) including some Zaynich pre-launch cost; biosimilars and India branded grow fastest; UK flat. Zaynich EBITDA -Rs60 / -45 / +100 cr: management guides a slight loss or neutral for 12-18 months from launch and breakeven by month 12-18; we assume a US team plus operating partner, India and EM launch costs of ~Rs80 cr in FY27E rising to ~Rs360 cr by FY29E against an ~80% gross margin.

assumptions._marginWhy: 19.62% / 19.62% / 21.76% = the base business (21.3% / 21.8% / 22.3%) and Zaynich (-Rs60 / -45 / +100 cr), see businessLines.margin. Reported EBITDA keeps excluding most R&D because NCE development is capitalised (FY26: ~10% of revenue spent, 3.6% expensed); the cost returns as amortisation (depreciation line). Each 1pp of FY28E margin is ~Rs45 cr of EBITDA, ~10% of FY28E EPS.
assumptions._capexWhy: ICRA (21-May-2026): capex ~Rs300 cr in each of FY27-28 (incl. NCE development it counts as capex), funded by internal accruals and Rs162 cr of unused QIP money; chairman (4-Jun-2026): normal capex Rs200-300 cr a year for three years, mainly biologics capacity, plus R&D at about the same share of sales. Rs300 / 320 / 340 cr.
assumptions._depWhy: Base depreciation only (Zaynich amortisation is carried separately, see interest): FY26 Rs227 cr; Q1FY27 Rs55 cr (Rs220 cr a year), growing with capex. 3.45% on gross block (Rs6,164 cr at Mar-26 plus capex) gives Rs218 / 229 / 240 cr.

otherTreasury._why: Three non-operating items Screener leaves inside other assets / other liabilities, moved out of working capital into the net cash line (AR FY26 balance sheet and notes 9, 40, 42): (1) the 14.15% minority in Wockhardt Bio AG, Rs341 cr at book, a claim on consolidated assets, so the EV/EBITDA and DCF cross-checks value only the owners' share; (2) net deferred tax assets Rs440 cr (Rs477 cr incl. Rs196 cr MAT credit, less Rs37 cr deferred tax liabilities), which cut future cash taxes that the engine otherwise pays in full; (3) assets held for sale Rs91 cr. Net +Rs190 cr. Without this the engine's working capital would be 49.9% of revenue (it would carry the DTA and the minority as operating items) instead of 34.1%. Model opening net debt = borrowings Rs2,233 cr (incl. Rs108 cr leases and ~Rs950 cr promoter loans) - cash Rs250 cr - investments Rs412 cr - Rs190 cr = Rs1,381 cr.

assumptions._treasuryWhy: The engine applies the yield only to positive net cash; the model's net cash stays negative (net debt ~Rs1.6-1.9k cr) in all three years, so treasury income is entered in otherIncome on gross liquid funds instead.

FY27E Rs74 cr = Q1FY27 actual Rs31 cr + three quarters at the FY25-26 recurring run-rate (~Rs14.5 cr a quarter). FY28E Rs60 cr and FY29E Rs62 cr = the recurring base (treasury income on ~Rs470 cr of liquid funds at ~6% is ~Rs28 cr of it). TTM to Jun-26 Rs122 cr includes the Rs55 cr of asset-sale profit (Rs67 cr without it).
assumptions._interestWhy: Finance cost Rs205 / 190 / 175 cr plus Zaynich amortisation Rs22 / 88 / 88 cr (see zaynichAmortisation). Finance cost: FY26 Rs213 cr (leases Rs11 cr); Q1FY27 Rs52 cr; external repayments of Rs171 cr (FY27) and Rs198 cr (FY28) per ICRA plus some reduction of ~Rs950 cr of promoter loans (5.9-12.3%). Refinancing at the improved A- rating is upside.
assumptions._taxWhy: FY26 effective rate 16.3% (Rs118 cr of tax losses used with no deferred tax created); Q1FY27 ~8%. Wockhardt Ltd still files under the old regime (34.9%) with Rs196 cr of MAT credit and loss carry-forwards; overseas profits are taxed at 12.5-25%. As the unrecognised losses run out the rate rises: 12% / 18% / 22%. The size of the remaining loss pool is not disclosed (gap).

dcf._betaWhy: Ke 13.4%: a single-asset launch (Zaynich) by a company with no US commercial record, three Indian sites still under USFDA import alert, a decade of losses until FY25, promoter pledges and promoter loans. Debt is ~5% of enterprise value, so the cost of equity is used as the discount rate (engine limit, PLAYBOOK §7).

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: Turnaround rule (PLAYBOOK §7c, decided 24-Nov-2026): earnings broke from losses to profit in the Jul-Sep 2025 quarter (PBT Rs91 cr, the first of four profitable quarters), the same day the Zaynich NDA was filed (30-Sep-2025), so Wockhardt's own window starts on 1-Oct-2025. Its one-year-forward P/E over the 52 weekly closes since then: median 66.7x (25th-75th 63.4-87.8x; forward EPS FY27E/FY28E, no exceptional items). Nine pharma peers' P/E moved +17.2% over the same window (sector-factor.js --from 2025-10-01; +17.2%). 66.7x x 1.172 = 78.2x, nearest half-turn 78x on Sep-28E EPS. Bull 103x (75th percentile x factor), bear 74.5x (25th). Since-2021 median 67.5x (EPS before exceptional items, FY23-25 troughs out) x the five-year +8.2% = 73x is a sensitivity row.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Cross-check: own one-year-forward EV/EBITDA since 1-Oct-2025 (EV = market value + net debt incl. promoter loans and the Bio AG minority, less net deferred tax and assets held for sale; forward EBITDA FY27E/FY28E): median 31.3x x the peers' EV/EBITDA move over the same window (+6.7%) = 33.5x on Sep-28E EBITDA; bull 39.5x, bear 32x.

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF at 13.4% (cost of equity used as the discount rate; debt ~5% of EV), terminal growth 5.5%, margin fading to 26%, plus the model's net debt (incl. promoter loans and the Bio AG minority at book) at Mar-27E.

assumptions._zaynichAmortisationWhy: Zaynich intangible Rs1,055 cr at Mar-26 (~Rs1,150 cr with FY27 spend); the AR says it will be capitalised by FY28; we assume from launch (~Jan-2027), straight-line over ~13 years (between the 2038 patent expiry and a 15-year life): ~Rs88 cr a year, Rs22 cr in FY27E. ENGINE WORKAROUND: the engine has one depreciation rate on gross block and holds CWIP (where Screener carries the intangible under development) flat, so it cannot show a step-up in amortisation; a single compromise rate would overstate FY27E and understate FY28-29E, which alone moved the target by ~13% (it feeds both the forward P/E history and Sep-28E EPS). We therefore add the amortisation to the finance-cost input (labelled), so EPS is right in each year; EBITDA, the EV/EBITDA cross-check and the DCF are unaffected.
